title: A conceptual framework of Intelligent Management Control System for Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how universities can better support management control, performance measurement, and strategic decision-making in a higher-education context. The authors argue that conventional management control systems are not well suited to universities because academic institutions have multi-stakeholder goals, long-term research and education missions, and complex information needs.

The paper proposes a conceptual framework for an Intelligent Management Control System for Higher Education (IMCSHE). The proposed system combines a Balanced Scorecard structure with artificial intelligence, specifically cognitive agents based on the LIDA architecture, and extends that architecture with a machine-learning module. The framework is designed to integrate data from multiple university information systems, such as employee evaluation, student/teaching systems, budgeting, publications, ERP, expenses control, project repositories, and infrastructure management, into a data warehouse and reporting layer.

The target context is higher education administration, especially university management and executive decision-making. The paper is not an empirical evaluation of an intervention; instead, it presents a design-science proposal and conceptual architecture intended to generate financial, customer, internal-process, and development reports for university leaders. The main conclusion is that an AI-enabled control system could improve scenario planning, reporting, and management support in universities, although this remains a proposed framework rather than a tested implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual framework paper with no empirical evaluation, no sample, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no measured outcomes. It does not provide evidence of effectiveness, only a proposed architecture and literature-grounded rationale.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact can be established because the paper does not report implementation results or outcome data. Any benefits are speculative and not supported by direct evidence in this article.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual framework for an Intelligent Management Control System for Higher Education (IMCSHE) using cognitive agents (LIDA) and a machine learning module to process university management data and generate Balanced Scorecard reports.

finding.finding_summary: This is a conceptual/design paper proposing an intelligent management control system for universities rather than testing outcomes empirically. The paper argues that combining a Balanced Scorecard with cognitive agents and machine learning could improve university management, scenario generation, and strategic decision support, but it reports no study sample, no comparison group, and no effect sizes.
finding.measure: Not empirically measured; conceptual architecture and proposed reporting/decision-support functions
